newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai, Philippine banks to sign repurchase pact.
newsitem.headline: Thai, Philippine banks to sign repurchase pact.

text.p: The central banks of Thailand and the Philippines will sign a bilateral agreement on Thursday that will help the two countries to cooperate to counter future market attack on their currencies.

Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond told reporters that the two central banks will sign a repurchase agreement, similar to other bilateral pacts Thailand has concluded with several other regional countries in past years.
Rerngchai said the Thai central bank would soon sign a similar $500 million repurchase agreement with China and plans to conclude a separate agreement on currency stabilisation with Japan later.
He said these bilateral agreements were for future contingencies but Thailand did not expect to have to use them in the near future because it could still rely on its large foreign reserves.

Central bank officials said Thailand's $38.7 billion foreign reserves were sufficient to finance more than six months of imports and could partly be used for the government to intervene to boost the baht.

The baht has weathered sporadic strong attacks in the past month stemming from rumours that Thailand may choose to devalue the currency later this year to help boost exports and curb the current account deficit.
Rerngchai said Thailand's foreign reserves were large enough for the country to ward off market pressure against the baht.
